verdicts.tldr: A collection registered by a sub-realm gets an index 'info' link that opens 'Unknown collection' instead of its page.
verdicts.details: Register only rejects prev.IsUser(), so a sub-realm registers, and its PkgPath is 'host#subpath' (uverse.go:251 subRealmSep = "#"). Line 204 builds infoLink := "/r/demo/defi/grc721reg:" + item.Key with the raw key, so the browser treats '#dao.SUB' as a fragment and Render receives only the host path, which Get misses. The hardcoded realm path half is weak: the realm lives at that fixed path, so only the '#' half costs a visitor anything. Fix: escape the key in the link (url.PathEscape or replace '#' with '%23') and add a sub-realm row to the render filetest.
verdicts.evidence: Read: grc721reg.gno:51 'if prev.IsUser() {' is the only identity gate; :204 'infoLink := "/r/demo/defi/grc721reg:" + item.Key'; uverse.go:251 'const subRealmSep = "#"'. Finder's filetest golden Output: '[info](/r/demo/defi/grc721reg:gno.land/r/demo/regsub#dao.SUB)' and 'Unknown collection: gno\.land/r/demo/regsub' for the fragment-cut path. Not re-run: read-only judge, the filetest has to be copied into the package to run.
verdicts.verify_by: Same filetest: the golden Output carries the info link with a raw '#' and the line 'Unknown collection: gno\.land/r/demo/regsub' for the cut path. | grep -n 'r/demo/defi/grc721reg' examples/gno.land/r/demo/defi/grc721reg/grc721reg.gno: one literal at line 204, no use of runtime.CurrentRealm().PkgPath()

verdicts.tldr: A collection with more than nine viewed kinds shows a badge set chosen by registration order, so two collections with the same kinds can show different badges.
verdicts.details: extensionBadges calls publishedKinds(v, maxBadges+1) with maxBadges = 8; publishedKinds takes token.ExtensionKindsUpTo(9), which walks tok.ledger.extensions in registration order and breaks at 9, and only then sorts. The sort orders the window but cannot choose it, so the comment's claim that output 'does not depend on the order the issuer registered them' holds only up to nine kinds. Fix: narrow the comment to the window, or sort the full (bounded) kind list before cutting it.
